title: Speed varies as the square root of linear size in swimming, flight and walking
look_for_in_this_kingdom: speeds inferred from trackways (dinosaur, early tetrapod, arthropod), stride length with limb length, fossil fish and flight reconstructions
variables_needed: measured speed per species or individual

claims.label: Speed varies as the square root of linear size in swimming, flight and walking
claims.statement: Leaving aside differences in mechanical construction, swimming (Froude's law), flight (minimum stable speed) and walking (the leg swinging as a pendulum) all give the same result: an animal's velocity tends to vary as the square root of its linear dimensions.
claims.quote: the general result, attained under very different conditions and arrived at by very different modes of reasoning, is in every case that the velocity tends to vary as the square root of the linear dimensions of the organism.
